question: Is the 64-boundary first-repeat miss specific to L % 64 == 0, or a general first-repeat race?  Does a delay remove it?  Does an intervening request remove it?
headline: Only prompts whose length is an exact multiple of 64 miss on the immediately following repeat; every other length hits immediately.
mechanism: not insert latency and not a request-triggered flush: 0.25-2.0 s of delay and an intervening unrelated request both leave the miss at 100%, while a second identical repeat hits 10/10 at the tax-law value. The prefix becomes reusable only after it has been prefilled twice -- one wasted full prefill per new multiple-of-64 prefix

design.cold_isolation: make_salt(seed) -> three fixed-width 4-letter marker words at the front of message 0; every trial's marker is unique and never reused, and every cold role that reports cached != 0 is retried
design.exact_lengths: body sized 12 tokens short of the target plus a one-token tail (' the' repeated); achieved prompt_tokens read back from every response and the cell is refused unless it equals the target
design.miss_definition: full_miss = cached == 0 on the repeat; partial = 0 < cached < 64*floor((L-1)//64); hit = cached == 64*floor((L-1)/64)
design.serial: one request in flight; no flock; POST /flush_cache never called

budget.note: phase 1 wrote its rows before a send() signature bug stopped the driver after the sweep; phases 2-3 were run by u10_phase23.py so the sweep was not re-spent

request_number_law.at_multiples_of_64: 1st request: cold (cached=0); 2nd identical request: cached=0 and full prefill, even after a 2 s delay or an intervening request; 3rd identical request: full tax-law hit
request_number_law.at_non_multiples: 1st cold, 2nd identical request: full tax-law hit (0/15 misses)

explains.U9_1024_case: yes, exactly: L=1024 is a multiple of 64 and reproduced at 5/5, with the second repeat recovering the tax-law hit (960)
explains.U4b_branch_2_case: no, not by the boundary rule: U4b's fan-out prompts were ~1925 tokens (1925 % 64 = 5), a residue class where this sweep saw 0/15 misses on identical repeats.  U4b's branch differed from branch 1 in its suffix (prefix-sharing, not an identical repeat); a pilot probe of that shape (same body, different tail, sent immediately) also reported cached=0, so it is plausibly the same insert-visibility class, but that shape is NOT covered by these n=5 cells.

operational_warning: A workload whose prompt length is an exact multiple of 64 pays one full prefill per new prefix: 10/10 immediate repeats at 1024 and 1088 tokens reported cached=0 and paid cold-prefill TTFT (median 263-533 ms at 1024 vs ~80 ms for a hit), and neither a 2 s delay nor an unrelated request in between removed it.  The same prompt sent a second time becomes reusable (rep2 10/10 at the tax-law value).
limits: n=5 per cell: each individual cell's CI is wide (0/5 -> [0, 0.52]); the claim rests on the pooled 10/10 vs 0/15 contrast, not on one cell.

The sweep covers 1008, 1023, 1024, 1025, 1088 tokens.  960, 1020, 1028, 1152, 2048 and 4096 were in the card's list and were not run: the 160-request bound was partly spent on 39 pilot probes that were needed to build an exact-length harness (see u10_pilot.json).
Only identical repeats are measured in the n=5 cells; the prefix-sharing (different suffix) shape that U4b hit is covered by one pilot probe only.

No file lock was taken (by instruction), so other units' traffic can interleave; every trial's cold role is verified cold, and the effect is binary rather than marginal, which makes eviction an implausible explanation for a 10/10 vs 0/15 split.
